Hi Patricia — great to hear procurement is moving this along. I put together a concise methodology and an initial commercial banding to get the conversation started. High level here, and I attached the longer PDF with examples and the pricing matrix.

Measurement methodology (summary):
- Token/measurement definition: we use model tokenizer tokens (BPE/byte-level) tied to the model version pinned in the commit (token counts will be normalized across variants).
- Test harness: Redwood provides a load generator (open-source) + a reference trace collector. You run an acceptance test that replays a representative production trace and a synthetic burst profile. We recommend two phases: 
  a) Stabilization (30m warm-up with production-like trace)
  b) Acceptance run (2–4 hours under steady-state load to verify sustained TPS and latency tails)
- Metrics captured: tokens/sec (aggregate and per-request), requests/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency (server-side), error rate, and GPU utilization.
- Acceptance criteria: sustained tokens/sec at >= 95% of committed rate for the 2–4 hour window; p95 latency <= agreed target for the pinned model and prompt size; no more than 0.5% error rate. Missed SLA triggers credit calculus in SOW.

SLA shape & burst behavior:
- Committed sustained throughput (C): our baseline guarantee (e.g., 150k tokens/sec).
- Short burst allowance (B): up to 1.5x C for spikes <= 60s, subject to cluster headroom and fair-share with other customers on the Dedicated instance if in a multi-tenant configuration (for fully reserved private pools this is higher).
- Degradation policy: if sustained usage exceeds C for > 10 minutes, automated throttling/fallback to best-effort model variant occurs unless explicit burst capacity is purchased.

Latency targets (example for reference models):
- For responses <= 512 tokens: p50 60–120ms, p95 <= 200–350ms depending on model/quantization; we will specify the target per-model in the SOW.
- For responses <= 1024 tokens: expect ~1.3–1.8x the 512-token latency; p95 targets are relaxed accordingly.

Commercial banding (summary):
- 6-month commit: baseline price, 10% discount at commit >= 50k tokens/sec, 18% at >= 100k tokens/sec.
- 12-month commit: +4% discount at each band (i.e., 14% and 22%).
- Add-on: guaranteed burst pool (B) purchase + fixed monthly fee to raise short-burst headroom.

I've attached: redwood_dedicated_sla_methodology_v1.pdf (methodology + examples) and commits_pricing_matrix.xlsx (example bands & breakout).

If that works, we can run through an acceptance-run plan with Rishi and then send a DocuSign SOW for signatures.

Best,

Ben/Evelyn/Laura — confirmed. Notes from infra validation:
- Model pinning: acceptance must use the exact model artifact specified in the SOW (hash checked). We provide a small checksum script and recommend storing signed logs (sha256) from the loadgen host.
- EdgeScale-hosted loadgen: acceptable as long as the runbook is followed and Redwood receives the raw logs + signed checksum + a short metadata JSON (run start/end times, model hash, config).
- Determinism: within a 2–4 hour steady-state run we see <5% variance in sustained tokens/sec across repeats for matched traces; latency p95 variance is typically 8–12% depending on burst noise. The SOW should therefore: 
  a) define an acceptance window (2–4 hours) and require two independent runs within 3 business days if results are borderline;
  b) allow a one-time remediation window to tune autoscaling/batch settings before final acceptance.

I'll finalize the acceptance_runbook.md with the exact artifact list and S3 upload instructions by EOD tomorrow and link the template in the DocuSign package.

Rishi
